subject: E-Commerce
title: Google Shopping's Failed Marketplace
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Google Shopping's Failed Marketplace.

hook.text: Google tried to build a marketplace six times and failed six times. Search dominance doesn't translate to shopping.

buildup.text: Google Froogle, Product Search, Shopping Express, Buy on Google, Shopping Actions—all launched and shut down.

discovery.text: Google is great at directing traffic TO stores but terrible at being a store. Commerce requires logistics, not links.

twist.text: Google now positions itself as a price comparison engine instead. It sends traffic to merchants rather than competing.

climax.text: Google's failures prove that marketplace success requires more than traffic. Trust, logistics, and payments must align.

punchline.text: Six attempts, six failures. Google can send you to a store but can't be one.

quiz.question: Why did Google's marketplace attempts repeatedly fail?
options: E-commerce requires logistics, trust, and payments—not just search traffic
